author: Navid Pez
title: Mr
text:
Mr
Review: YouTube App & Remote Control Experience
Rating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️ (3/5 Stars)
The Good: Finding Your Remote via Phone App
One of the most genuinely useful features built into the modern smart TV and streaming ecosystem is the ability to track down a lost physical remote using your phone.
 How it works: When your phone is connected to the same Wi-Fi network and paired with the YouTube app or your TV platform (like Google TV or Apple TV), you can often trigger a "Find My Remote" ping or simply use your phone as an instant, fully functional replacement remote.
 Verdict: It saves you from tearing apart the couch cushions and provides a seamless backup when the physical clicker goes missing.
The Frustrating: The Random Screen Disconnection Bug
Unfortunately, the streaming experience takes a major hit due to a persistent and baffling bug: the remote control randomly disconnecting the screen/session while watching YouTube.
 The Problem: Even when you are paying for an active YouTube Premium membership, the app frequently drops the connection between your mobile device/remote and the TV screen. Mid-video, the cast drops, the interface desyncs, or the screen blanks out, forcing you to reconnect and navigate back to what you were watching.
 Why it hurts: Paid memberships are supposed to offer an uninterrupted, premium viewing experience free of friction. Dealing with random disconnects breaks the flow and makes the remote pairing feel unreliable.
Final Thoughts
The convenience of using your phone as a backup remote is fantastic, but the software stability on the YouTube casting and remote-pairing side leaves a lot to be desired. Until Google patches out these random disconnection bugs—especially for paying members—the experience remains a frustrating mix of smart features and glitchy execution.

author: S.R. S
title: Shame on Samsung
text:
Shame on Samsung
Samsung sold my  $700 tablet and specifically promoted SmartThings compatibility. My tablet still works great, but Samsung abandoned its update support since 2022 and locked it out of the Smartthings ecosystem it was sold to control. I wonder if they do this in Korea too, or if it’s just a way to pick the pockets of Americans. Europe is fighting back against this theft with regulation. America should too. 

This is money-hungry corporate-engineered obsolescence: a greedy plan to slowly cripple expensive, perfectly fine hardware to force customers into buying replacements. Samsung charges premium prices, then treats its products—and customers—as disposable. 

Shame on Samsung. I left its ecosystem for Apple because of this. 

Don’t accept these practices—report them to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. New Yorkers can also file a consumer complaint with the New York Attorney General.

title: Where quality is job … well, it might be on the list
text:
Where quality is job … well, it might be on the list
They put a notice in the app saying there was a warranty extension offer, but after filling out a form with information they already have it says our washer wasn’t eligible. Wasting everyone’s time because they’re too lazy to filter notifications based on the devices you actually own is basically what using this app is like all the time. 

The setup process is very clumsy and they constantly lie about privacy (no, high-precision background location tracking on your phone is not needed to put a washing machine online). 

The app sometimes hangs on load, requiring you to use the reset data option, force quit, and restart it to load anything. 

It nags constantly about setting up MFA but still only supports the text messaging stuff hackers routinely break despite easier to use, more secure FIDO alternatives being in their second decade.

title: 아주 좋아요!
text:
아주 좋아요!
너무 만족하면서 사용하고 있습니다. 다만 로봇청소기와 관련해 두 가지 개선되었으면 하는 점이 있어 건의드립니다.

첫째, 물걸레 세척 주기를 현재처럼 15분 단위가 아니라 1분 단위로 설정할 수 있으면 좋겠습니다. 집 전체를 청소하면 약 30분 정도 소요되는데, 가끔 31분 정도 걸리는 경우가 있습니다. 이때 청소가 거의 끝난 시점인데도 물걸레를 다시 세척한 뒤 잠깐만 청소하고 바로 복귀하는 경우가 있어 조금 비효율적으로 느껴졌습니다.

둘째, 로봇청소기 필터는 보통 10회 정도 사용하면 청소 알림이 뜨는데, 필터를 직접 청소한 후 사용자가 알림을 초기화하거나 재설정할 수 있는 기능이 있으면 더욱 편리할 것 같습니다.

이 두 가지 사항만 개선된다면 더욱 만족스럽게 사용할 수 있을 것 같습니다. 좋은 어플 만들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

author: Toasted-Ravioli
title: Push Notification Ads Instead of Reliable Appliances
text:
Push Notification Ads Instead of Reliable Appliances
I have this app for one reason. I want to know when my food is done and when my laundry is ready to be pulled out. That's it.

So why am I getting daily push notifications about a folding phone I never asked about?

I keep hopping into the settings looking for a way to turn off the ads and keep the alerts for the devices I paid a lot of money for. I've toggled off just about everything I could find. It's still happening every day, going on a week and a half. So my options are apparently to take the ads or turn off notifications entirely, which kills the whole point of the app. I'm not the only one, either. The forums are full of people asking the same thing.

I wish that energy went somewhere useful. My washing machine bills itself as making my life easier and it constantly clogs itself with lint. It's the most high maintenance washer I've ever owned. But the real innovation Samsung seems to be figuring out is how to turn people who already bought your stuff into a captive audience for more of it.

All I am trying to do is connect one lousy refrigerator that is a simple and plain refrigerator. No touch screen or anything fancy. All that for a lousy refrigerator. That is crazy!  So why does Samsung need to constantly know your location and all that other information? Easy, to gather information about people to make money off of it. Samsung, Google, Facebook and others make a lot of money from selling people’s information. So I did what every privacy concern citizen would do, returned the refrigerator and got me a GE. 
Seriously Samsung, stop spaying on people to make a profit. People are already paying for your devices, it’s not like we are getting them for free.

author: Iratherfly
title: Never works -clunky nonsense
text:
Never works -clunky nonsense
I’m using the latest iPhone Pro with iOS 26, and like all phones and OS versions before that, Endless looking for devices, spinning wheel of my life wasting away, blank dark screens that the only way to get out of is by crashing the app. And all of this for what? So I can use it as a remote for my smart TV? No, so I can connect a remote using it to my TV, or buy all kinds of useless Samsung house automation gadgets, most of which not supported in the US market or already have better devices from other companies.  The reason I love using Apple devices is that they’re fluid and work together, mostly flawlessly, they also work well with Google devices and things from other brands. I don’t have to set 1000 settings and have a course in what each cryptic or internally branded option does for things that should just work. That is not saving me time or effort.

Samsung devices are very capable on paper, but in order to receive the coveted Samsung logo, they must first go through rigorous testing to guarantee a hellish level of miserable user experience. You would think over the years there will be incentive by to fix it because the world moves forward but no, they just double down on making it worse every time.

author: another ex customer
title: Ultimate FAIL
text:
Ultimate FAIL
I ordered a Samsung (Model: DW 90F89 POUSRAA) Dishwasher from Best Buy, July 23rd. It was  delivered and installed on July 3rd. Didn’t wash one load of dishes before we got an error code to turn off power to the dishwasher (which means most of the kitchen). On July 6th a repairman came and said it wasn’t the installation, that the dishwasher, itself, was leaking from the bottom. Best Buy set up an appointment for July 17 to replace the dishwasher, uninstall the broken one and install a NEW NEW dishwasher. After confirming the appt. July 16 in the evening, they called at 8:17am to say “Nope, won’t be there. Our next available date is July 27th to uninstall the malfunctioning dishwasher and install the NEW NEW dishwasher. Now, we wait to see if that actually happens 35 days after they took our money. If you had offered 0 stars I would have given that rating.

title: Needs a lot of improvement
text:
Needs a lot of improvement
First off, I would like to say that the remote interface is ridiculous, the arrow buttons are absolutely tiny with the SELECT button being a gigantic pad, it would be better if the interface was more balanced and looked closer to the actual remote layout. I understand they are trying to utilize a swipe feature for this ginormous pad, but it doesn’t even work right and many apps don’t support it, so it’s useless. I also don’t like how there’s no way to turn on the TV using the app. How is it that other apps such as YouTube or airplay can turn on the TV by just selecting the name of the device, yet this app, that is designed by Samsung, can’t? When it comes to pairing the app to the TV, you need to navigate the TV settings to find a specific code and approving of terms I believe, which requires needing a physical remote. If you’re like me, and I’m sure majority of downloaders, you’re getting this app because you either don’t have the remote, can’t find it, or it is broken. Again, why is it that the app AirPlay can display the code to link the TV automatically without the need for navigation and this Samsung app can’t? Terms can easily be accepted on the app itself also. Samsung, please take notes from AirPlay for pairing/turning on the TV from the app and redesign the layout or at least given an option for an alternate remote layout that doesn’t have tiny navigation buttons and a ginormous select button.

author: BVRacingOO7
title: Family Hub Fridge Manger Issue
text:
Family Hub Fridge Manger Issue
After about two years of ownership, the Fridge Manager app on my refrigerator started having issues. It began with the water filter replacement indicator—the reset function stopped working. A few months later, the Family Hub lost its network connection, which caused the Fridge Manager app to become unusable. The app would freeze, preventing me from managing any of the refrigerator’s settings, and every time I tapped on it, it would immediately return to the home screen.

Unfortunately, the technicians were unable to repair the issue because it requires replacing the entire Family Hub rather than fixing a single component. For newer models, the replacement costs approximately $1,300 or more, making it a very expensive repair.

Overall, I really like the refrigerator and its features, but this experience was disappointing considering the cost of the appliance. If you’re planning to purchase a Family Hub model, I strongly recommend investing in an extended warranty or protection plan. It could save you from a significant out-of-pocket expense if the Family Hub fails after the manufacturer’s warranty expires.

title: New Updates Trash
text:
New Updates Trash
Overall, I enjoy this refrigerator, but some of the smart features need improvement. The Ring Doorbell integration is unreliable (stop working), and navigating the main screen and TV interface feels clunky and could use a more intuitive layout.

My biggest disappointment is the recent photo update. One of the main reasons I bought this refrigerator was to display family photos. The old photo gallery, which showed multiple photos and automatically scrolled through them, was much better. The new full-screen display feels more like a billboard than a digital photo album. Please bring back the previous photo gallery feature.

title: Major bugs with iOS 26.5.1 and 26.5.2 — cannot add Samsung Lennox mini split
text:
Major bugs with iOS 26.5.1 and 26.5.2 — cannot add Samsung Lennox mini split
I had a Lennox mini split air conditioner by Samsung installed two weeks ago. The installer was not able to get the mini split to connect to smartThings on my phone. We encountered many errors along the way. I tried troubleshooting over the next two weeks unsuccessfully, with the process always failing on the last step, which is “registering” the product. Yesterday my Lennox dealer sent their very knowledgeable tech-support person as well as their installation supervisor, to help. For over two hours, he tried to troubleshoot the connectivity with my phone. He was also a user of SmartThings with his own mini split at his own home, and after trying every possible scenario many times, we discovered that this problem occurs only if you have the latest two iOS versions. I was on iOS 26.5.1, which was released a month after the latest SmartThings v 1.7.46 release date which currently says was two months ago. My tech-support person was on an older version at his home which worked fine. He then downloaded the new iOS 26.5.2 onto his phone and was no longer able to connect his mini split (or mine) after he had disconnected it for our testing. (As part of our testing process, he was able to successfully connect his SmartThings app in his phone to my mini split and fully control it when he was on his older version of iOS). Specifically, these are the steps that happen in the app: a mini split is successfully scanned and recognized by the app; it gets past a that says connecting to device; it then allows me to select my Wi-Fi network; and then it gets to a page that says “registering your device.” That’s where things fall apart. author: g0akc
title: Great but can be unreliable especially geo location
text:
Great but can be unreliable especially geo location
Update 27th June:
I might have now fixed my geo location issues which were causing false intruder alarms - it thought everyone had left the house when a person (their iPhone) was still inside.  It seems to be a known bug to do with it remembering just one on a first out/in basis.  Looking on ‘my smart things’ advanced via a browser I identified our iPhones.  I gave them specific names.  The locations were being tracked correctly on there (presenceSensor set to present or not present depending on iPhone at home or away. So it appeared to be a bug Samsung’s end.  We opened the app and turned off use phone location simultaneously. I deleted the automatic routines ‘Home’ and ‘Away’ used to arm/disarm the alarm system.  Turned location back on both phones. Recreated the routines with AND or OR logic (ALL members leave, ANY member returns home).  Tested briefly by taking my phone out of the home zone then back.  Seen in ‘my smartthings’.  Fingers crossed - I wait to see what happens when my wife leaves home (I don’t want to take her phone for a walk as it’s personal to her) and very hot here!

Review 25th June 26: Recently SmartThings has lost the location of my iPhone.  This has lead to our intruder alarm sounding while I was still in the house!  It took my wife leaving (with her iPhone) as ‘everyone has left’ (I have routines set to arm the system if we both leave and to disarm if any one of us arrives home).  I have tried various things to fix this and all settings appear correct.  I have even reset  ‘privacy and location’ on the iPhone as well as reinstalling the app several times.  My wife has just gone out and yet again it armed the alarm saying we had all left - my phone and I are still in the house!  I shall have to disable the routines and set it manually.

title: 사용기 및 개선 건의 사항
text:
사용기 및 개선 건의 사항
삼성 전자 제품 연동해서 잘 사용하고 있어요. 절약 기능 상시 켜놓구 상황에 따라 자동화도하구 루틴도 하구요. 또 확장된 기능을 제공하는 서드파티 제조사들 제품도 연동되고 점점 많아져서 더 좋아요. 
최근에는 지그비 기능으로  외부에서도 전등류도 센서 연동해서 많이 사용하는데 너무 편해지고 좋네요. 
이렇게 몇개월 넘게 사용해보니 몇가지 중요한 개선 요청 드릴내용이 있어요. 검토햐주시면 감사하겠습니다. 
1. 지그비로 전등 자동화 구성시에 loT 마그네틱 전등 기능중에 점점 밝게와 점점 어둡게 설정이 가능해요. 하지만 예를들어 설정시간 5분동안 밝기만 어둡게 / 밝게 조정하고 싶은데 색온도를 함께 넣어줘야 기능을 쓸수 있네요. 이부분 개선되면 지하 주차장 처럼 사람이 없을땐 에너지 절약을 위해 50% 센서 감지되면 100% 색온도 설정없이 순수 밝기만 조정하면 좋겠습니다. 
2. 다른 하나는 IoT 전등은 대부분모두 색온도 설정이 가능한데 조정 가능 범위가 2700k부터 가능하게 되어 있어요. 실제로 대부분 전등들은 보다 넒게 가능한 경우가 많아요. 이를 사용자가 좀더 넓게 2000k 부터로 설정할수 있으면 편의성이 올라가고 훨씬 만족 스럽게 사용할거라 생각되네요. 
이두가지 내용들 추후 업데이트 반영 기대해 봅니다. 가능할까요?

author: LadfromYork
title: Okay but limited functionality
text:
Okay but limited functionality
It’s useful to be able to control my heating and hot water, in terms of turning it in or off. 

However that is it in terms of functionality. I can’t do anything more useful such as setting schedules for when I want the heating and hot water to go on and off. For example, I would like to reduce the temperature after a certain point in the evening, but have it rise again before I get up in the morning.

Strangely Samsung don’t have the concept of an air sourced heat pump in the devices category, it has to be classed as an air conditioning unit. Maybe once they realise these things have been around for a while (they do make them), they may improve the limited functionality.

There may be more functionality than I realise but the user interface is such a poor experience in terms of it not being obvious what to tap next, that I may have missed some things.

I’ve dropped it further to one star because it nags for a rating almost every time I use it.

author: S2Mil
title: Huge app thirsty for access and complicated setup (failed)
text:
Huge app thirsty for access and complicated setup (failed)
I was forced to install this app just to use my TV, which already felt unnecessary. The app takes up nearly 1GB of space and appears to fail the setup process if you decline any of the numerous permission requests.

During setup, the process broke at the step where my phone was supposed to automatically transfer Wi-Fi details to the TV. This never happened, yet the app displayed misleading instructions suggesting I needed to take manual action—when in fact, there was nothing I could do. I was effectively stuck and had to find a workaround on my own.

After a lengthy and frustrating setup, I’m left with a TV that has limited functionality, along with concerns about my personal data being spread across devices without clear control or transparency.

The only positive aspect is that some setup steps were quite detailed and even adapted to my specific phone model, which shows potential—but it doesn’t make up for the overall experience.

title: Constantly fails to connect to Frame TV
text:
Constantly fails to connect to Frame TV
I really want to like this app. It has huge potential and IMO is more sophisticated than HomeKit, Google Home, etc. Now that Matter is a reality, I want this to be my go-to app for smart home control. The energy saving section is well thought out, with huge potential… 

However, it is very disappointing that this Samsung app doesn’t work reliably with the flagship Samsung Frame TV - especially when trying to control the subscription art. 

Constant errors, disconnections and freezing result in anger and frustration. I really hope they find a way to make their own products compatible… at the moment, it just doesn’t work well enough, online forums are full of complaints, and Samsung should be embarrassed!

…6 months later, it is still completely unreliable. The Samsung Frame TV that acts as a Samsung hub does not have an Ethernet port and has a network connection failure every few days. I don’t understand how Samsung can promise so much but deliver so little!

——————-
July 2025 Update

Trying to control a Frame TV is a constant struggle. 

Persistent pop-ups asking to me to activate microphone so Samsung can push more advertising.

I purchased an art Frame TV to frame art, but the options are very limited and the interface is constantly trying to force me to watch Samsung TV. What I want is to control art, and use Routines relevant to displaying art. That’s why I purchased an Art TV. I am so sick of their contempt for their own customers.

——-

Also pretty pointless for microwave ovens. 

User guide just takes you to a generic page on the website where you have to choose region, language, then search for country, appliance category etc. useless!

Cannot pre-set a cooking mode, cannot control remotely. Oven constantly loses date and time and re-sync can only be done manually. It’s the dumbest smart thing I ever used!

title: Cook with your ingredients feature is amateur at best - easy to fix
text:
Cook with your ingredients feature is amateur at best - easy to fix
The cook with your ingredients is a gimmick as you can only filter by one ingredient. I’ve contact Samsung several times through here and by email, I’m a developer myself and all they need to do to make this feature actually valuable is allow multiple filters. 

At the moment if I have chicken, peppers and onions in the fridge I can only search recipes with chicken OR peppers OR onions. Why can’t I select multiple and give me recipes that include chicken AND peppers AND onions. 

It’s a very simple school level filter, which Samsung don’t seem capable to firstly identify, and secondly develop. 

It’s very frustrating as I use this feature a few times a week. 

Please can someone fix this, it’s a quick win that will make this feature usable for everybody.

On the whole the devices work brilliantly, but the app could be improved with little additional design effort.
